// @effect-v4
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics promiseAllInEffect:warning
import { Data, Effect, pipe } from "effect"
import * as Eff from "effect/Effect"

interface User {
  readonly name: string
}

class FetchError extends Data.TaggedError("FetchError")<{ readonly cause: unknown }> {}

declare const ids: ReadonlyArray<string>
declare const mutableIds: Array<string>
declare const fetchUser: (id: string) => Promise<User>
declare const fetchUserWithSignal: (id: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<User>
declare const load: () => Promise<void>
declare const extra: Promise<User>
declare const pending: ReadonlyArray<Promise<User>>
declare const nonEmptyPending: readonly [Promise<User>, ...Array<Promise<User>>]
declare const pendingSet: Set<Promise<User>>
declare const anything: any
declare const idPage: { readonly map: <B>(f: (id: string) => B) => Array<B> }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: the issue's examples (Effect.promise / Effect.tryPromise thunks).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.all over xs.map(inline arrow) as the whole tryPromise thunk body.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const users = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled over xs.map(identifier). No quick fix (allSettled never gets one).
export const settled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: thunk-safe shape, quick fix offered.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.promise thunk, inline arrow callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseArrow = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: inline function expression callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => { return fetchUser(id) }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFunctionExpression = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.map(function(id) {
    return fetchUser(id)
  }))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: callback uses the index; Effect.forEach passes (item, index) too.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id, i) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithIndex = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i) => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: mutable array input.
export const promiseMutableArray = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(mutableIds.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: the mapped expression is itself a chain; it becomes the forEach input.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0), (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFilteredInput = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0).map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the thunk forwards its `signal`; the concurrency bound is still missing.
// Quick fix redeclares `signal` on each per-item thunk:
// Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithSignal = Effect.promise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: same with Effect.tryPromise and fetch's options object.
export const tryPromiseWithSignal = Effect.tryPromise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetch(`https://example.com/users/${id}`, { signal })))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import from "effect/Effect".
export const namespaceImport = Eff.forEach(ids, id => Eff.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })

// MUST TRIGGER: async inline callback; the per-item thunk keeps the callback's `async` modifier
// (same for an `async function` expression callback).
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(async () => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const asyncCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(async (id) => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name })))

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk inside a data-last Effect.flatMap in a `.pipe(...)` chain.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(xs, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const inPipeFlatMap = Effect.succeed(ids).pipe(Effect.flatMap((xs) => Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(xs.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: reported, but outside the thunk-safe shape, so no quick fix.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier callback (xs.map(fetchUser)); no quick fix.
export const identifierCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST TRIGGER: map callback declares 3 parameters; no quick fix. Effect.forEach passes only
// (item, index), so a callback that declares a third parameter does not type-check after the rewrite.
export const mapWithArrayParam = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i, all) => fetchUser(`${i}/${all.length}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: `.map` is not Array.prototype.map; no quick fix. The receiver is not iterable,
// so `Effect.forEach(idPage, ...)` would not compile.
export const nonArrayMap = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(idPage.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: argument is an array variable, not xs.map(...); no quick fix.
export const arrayVariable = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: tuple with a rest element (`[...Promise<User>[], Promise<User>]`); no quick fix.
export const restTupleSpread = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([...ids.map(fetchUser), extra]))

// MUST TRIGGER: declared non-empty tuple type (`readonly [Promise<User>, ...Promise<User>[]]`).
export const restTupleDeclared = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(nonEmptyPending))

// MUST TRIGGER: async thunk; no quick fix.
export const asyncThunk = Effect.tryPromise(async () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk; the call is not the whole (concise) body, no quick fix.
export const blockBodyThunk = Effect.promise(() => {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the Promise.all result is chained, so the call is not the whole body; no quick fix.
export const chainedResult = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))).then((values) => values.length))

// MUST TRIGGER: { try, catch } object form of Effect.tryPromise; no quick fix.
export const tryPromiseObject = Effect.tryPromise({
  try: () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled with an inline callback still gets no quick fix
// (the success type would change from PromiseSettledResult<A>[]).
export const settledInline = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: global Promise reached through a const alias.
const GlobalPromise = Promise
export const aliasedPromise = Effect.promise(() => GlobalPromise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: other Effect constructor thunks.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.sync thunk.
export const inSync = Effect.sync(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try thunk.
export const inTry = Effect.try(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try { try, catch } object form.
export const inTryObject = Effect.try({
  try: () => Promise.allSettled(pending),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.suspend thunk.
export const inSuspend = Effect.suspend(() => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.callback body.
export const inCallback = Effect.callback<ReadonlyArray<User>>((resume) => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  pendingAll.then((values) => resume(Effect.succeed(values)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk nested in a pipeline callback is still a thunk.
export const inForEachCallback = Effect.forEach(
  [ids, mutableIds],
  (group) => Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(group.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))),
  { concurrency: 1 }
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.gen and generator Effect.fn bodies.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const promises = ids.map(fetchUser)
  // MUST TRIGGER: bare Promise.all in a gen body (the promises start here, outside the Effect).
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled in a gen body.
  const settledAll = Promise.allSettled(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.promise thunk inside the gen body (argument is not xs.map(...), no quick fix).
  const users = yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(promises))
  // MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length tuple in a gen body.
  const pair = Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")])
  return { pendingAll, settledAll, users, pair }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn body.
export const inEffectFn = Effect.fn("inEffectFn")(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn without a span name.
export const inEffectFnAnonymous = Effect.fn(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(input.map(fetchUser)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fnUntraced body.
export const inEffectFnUntraced = Effect.fnUntraced(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length fan-out (tuple without a rest element).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: two-element literal is a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPair = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: allSettled over a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPairSettled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled([fetchUser("a"), load()]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `as const` fixed tuple.
export const fixedAsConst = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: empty tuple.
export const fixedEmpty = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: v1 only reports arrays and rest tuples; a Set is neither.
export const fromSet = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pendingSet))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `any` input is neither an array nor a tuple.
export const fromAny = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(anything))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: outside Effect-run code.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: top-level module code.
export const topLevel = Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: plain async function.
export async function plainAsync() {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): combinator inside a function nested in the thunk;
// the effect-context analysis resets at every function boundary.
export const nestedInThen = Effect.tryPromise(() => load().then(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))))

  return yield* Effect.promise(run)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try { try, catch } object form.
export const inTryObject = Effect.try({
  try: () => Promise.allSettled(pending),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.suspend thunk.
export const inSuspend = Effect.suspend(() => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.callback body.
export const inCallback = Effect.callback<ReadonlyArray<User>>((resume) => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  pendingAll.then((values) => resume(Effect.succeed(values)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk nested in a pipeline callback is still a thunk.
export const inForEachCallback = Effect.forEach(
  [ids, mutableIds],
  (group) => Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(group.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))),
  { concurrency: 1 }
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.gen and generator Effect.fn bodies.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const promises = ids.map(fetchUser)
  // MUST TRIGGER: bare Promise.all in a gen body (the promises start here, outside the Effect).
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled in a gen body.
  const settledAll = Promise.allSettled(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.promise thunk inside the gen body (argument is not xs.map(...), no quick fix).
  const users = yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(promises))
  // MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length tuple in a gen body.
  const pair = Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")])
  return { pendingAll, settledAll, users, pair }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn body.
export const inEffectFn = Effect.fn("inEffectFn")(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn without a span name.
export const inEffectFnAnonymous = Effect.fn(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(input.map(fetchUser)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fnUntraced body.
export const inEffectFnUntraced = Effect.fnUntraced(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length fan-out (tuple without a rest element).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: two-element literal is a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPair = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: allSettled over a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPairSettled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled([fetchUser("a"), load()]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `as const` fixed tuple.
export const fixedAsConst = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: empty tuple.
export const fixedEmpty = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: v1 only reports arrays and rest tuples; a Set is neither.
export const fromSet = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pendingSet))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `any` input is neither an array nor a tuple.
export const fromAny = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(anything))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: outside Effect-run code.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: top-level module code.
export const topLevel = Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: plain async function.
export async function plainAsync() {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): combinator inside a function nested in the thunk;
// the effect-context analysis resets at every function boundary.
export const nestedInThen = Effect.tryPromise(() => load().then(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): function nested in a gen body.
export const nestedInGenCallback = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const run = () => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))
  return yield* Effect.promise(run)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the thunk returns a function; Promise.all runs in that inner function.
export const thunkReturningFunction = Effect.sync(() => () => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free thunk; only direct thunk arguments are Effect context.
export const pointFreeThunk = pipe(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)), Effect.promise)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: non-generator Effect.fn body is not an Effect context.
export const nonGeneratorEffectFn = Effect.fn("nonGeneratorEffectFn")((input: ReadonlyArray<string>) => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
  return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll.then((values) => values.length))
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.runPromise wraps an Effect; Promise.all here is plain Promise code.
export const runOutside = () => Promise.all([Effect.runPromise(users), Effect.runPromise(settled)])
export const runOutsideArray = () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.runPromise(Effect.succeed(id))))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: not the global Promise.all / Promise.allSettled.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user function named `all`.
const all = <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => Promise.all(values)
export const userAll = Effect.promise(() => all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user object with `all` / `allSettled` methods.
const Batch = {
  all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => globalThis.Promise.all(values),
  allSettled: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.allSettled(values)
}
export const batchAll = Effect.promise(() => Batch.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
export const batchAllSettled = Effect.promise(() => Batch.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a local binding named `Promise` shadows the global.
export const shadowedPromise = (() => {
  const Promise = {
    all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<globalThis.Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.resolve(values.length)
  }
  return Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
})()

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Promise combinators (out of scope; see promiseRaceInEffect).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.race belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
export const race = Effect.promise(() => Promise.race(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.any belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
export const anyUser = Effect.promise(() => Promise.any(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.resolve over an array is not a fan-out.
export const resolved = Effect.promise(() => Promise.resolve(ids.map((id) => id.length)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the issue's good examples.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const goodUsers = Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: 8 })

export const goodSettled = Effect.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id))), {
  concurrency: 8,
  mode: "result"
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: one promise per Effect, the shape the quick fix produces.
export const goodUnbounded = Effect.forEach(
  ids,
  (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)),
  { concurrency: "unbounded" }
)

// @effect-v4
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics promiseAllInEffect:warning
import { Data, Effect, pipe } from "effect"
import * as Eff from "effect/Effect"

interface User {
  readonly name: string
}

class FetchError extends Data.TaggedError("FetchError")<{ readonly cause: unknown }> {}

declare const ids: ReadonlyArray<string>
declare const mutableIds: Array<string>
declare const fetchUser: (id: string) => Promise<User>
declare const fetchUserWithSignal: (id: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<User>
declare const load: () => Promise<void>
declare const extra: Promise<User>
declare const pending: ReadonlyArray<Promise<User>>
declare const nonEmptyPending: readonly [Promise<User>, ...Array<Promise<User>>]
declare const pendingSet: Set<Promise<User>>
declare const anything: any
declare const idPage: { readonly map: <B>(f: (id: string) => B) => Array<B> }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: the issue's examples (Effect.promise / Effect.tryPromise thunks).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.all over xs.map(inline arrow) as the whole tryPromise thunk body.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const users = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled over xs.map(identifier). No quick fix (allSettled never gets one).
export const settled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: thunk-safe shape, quick fix offered.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.promise thunk, inline arrow callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseArrow = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: inline function expression callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => { return fetchUser(id) }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFunctionExpression = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.map(function(id) {
    return fetchUser(id)
  }))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: callback uses the index; Effect.forEach passes (item, index) too.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id, i) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithIndex = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i) => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: mutable array input.
export const promiseMutableArray = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(mutableIds.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: the mapped expression is itself a chain; it becomes the forEach input.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0), (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFilteredInput = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0).map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the thunk forwards its `signal`; the concurrency bound is still missing.
// Quick fix redeclares `signal` on each per-item thunk:
// Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithSignal = Effect.promise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: same with Effect.tryPromise and fetch's options object.
export const tryPromiseWithSignal = Effect.tryPromise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetch(`https://example.com/users/${id}`, { signal })))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import from "effect/Effect".
export const namespaceImport = Eff.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: async inline callback; the per-item thunk keeps the callback's `async` modifier
// (same for an `async function` expression callback).
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(async () => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const asyncCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(async (id) => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name })))

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk inside a data-last Effect.flatMap in a `.pipe(...)` chain.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(xs, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const inPipeFlatMap = Effect.succeed(ids).pipe(Effect.flatMap((xs) => Effect.forEach(xs, id => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: reported, but outside the thunk-safe shape, so no quick fix.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier callback (xs.map(fetchUser)); no quick fix.
export const identifierCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST TRIGGER: map callback declares 3 parameters; no quick fix. Effect.forEach passes only
// (item, index), so a callback that declares a third parameter does not type-check after the rewrite.
export const mapWithArrayParam = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i, all) => fetchUser(`${i}/${all.length}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: `.map` is not Array.prototype.map; no quick fix. The receiver is not iterable,
// so `Effect.forEach(idPage, ...)` would not compile.
export const nonArrayMap = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(idPage.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: argument is an array variable, not xs.map(...); no quick fix.
export const arrayVariable = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: tuple with a rest element (`[...Promise<User>[], Promise<User>]`); no quick fix.
export const restTupleSpread = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([...ids.map(fetchUser), extra]))

// MUST TRIGGER: declared non-empty tuple type (`readonly [Promise<User>, ...Promise<User>[]]`).
export const restTupleDeclared = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(nonEmptyPending))

// MUST TRIGGER: async thunk; no quick fix.
export const asyncThunk = Effect.tryPromise(async () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk; the call is not the whole (concise) body, no quick fix.
export const blockBodyThunk = Effect.promise(() => {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the Promise.all result is chained, so the call is not the whole body; no quick fix.
export const chainedResult = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))).then((values) => values.length))

// MUST TRIGGER: { try, catch } object form of Effect.tryPromise; no quick fix.
export const tryPromiseObject = Effect.tryPromise({
  try: () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled with an inline callback still gets no quick fix
// (the success type would change from PromiseSettledResult<A>[]).
export const settledInline = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: global Promise reached through a const alias.
const GlobalPromise = Promise
export const aliasedPromise = Effect.promise(() => GlobalPromise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: other Effect constructor thunks.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const inSync = Effect.sync(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try thunk.

// @effect-v4
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics promiseAllInEffect:warning
import { Data, Effect, pipe } from "effect"
import * as Eff from "effect/Effect"

interface User {
  readonly name: string
}

class FetchError extends Data.TaggedError("FetchError")<{ readonly cause: unknown }> {}

declare const ids: ReadonlyArray<string>
declare const mutableIds: Array<string>
declare const fetchUser: (id: string) => Promise<User>
declare const fetchUserWithSignal: (id: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<User>
declare const load: () => Promise<void>
declare const extra: Promise<User>
declare const pending: ReadonlyArray<Promise<User>>
declare const nonEmptyPending: readonly [Promise<User>, ...Array<Promise<User>>]
declare const pendingSet: Set<Promise<User>>
declare const anything: any
declare const idPage: { readonly map: <B>(f: (id: string) => B) => Array<B> }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: the issue's examples (Effect.promise / Effect.tryPromise thunks).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.all over xs.map(inline arrow) as the whole tryPromise thunk body.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const users = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled over xs.map(identifier). No quick fix (allSettled never gets one).
export const settled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: thunk-safe shape, quick fix offered.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.promise thunk, inline arrow callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseArrow = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: inline function expression callback.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(() => { return fetchUser(id) }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFunctionExpression = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.map(function(id) {
    return fetchUser(id)
  }))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: callback uses the index; Effect.forEach passes (item, index) too.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id, i) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithIndex = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i) => fetchUser(`${i}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: mutable array input.
export const promiseMutableArray = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(mutableIds.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: the mapped expression is itself a chain; it becomes the forEach input.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0), (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseFilteredInput = Effect.promise(() =>
  Promise.all(ids.filter((id) => id.length > 0).map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the thunk forwards its `signal`; the concurrency bound is still missing.
// Quick fix redeclares `signal` on each per-item thunk:
// Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const promiseWithSignal = Effect.promise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: same with Effect.tryPromise and fetch's options object.
export const tryPromiseWithSignal = Effect.tryPromise((signal) =>
  Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetch(`https://example.com/users/${id}`, { signal })))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: namespace import from "effect/Effect".
export const namespaceImport = Eff.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: async inline callback; the per-item thunk keeps the callback's `async` modifier
// (same for an `async function` expression callback).
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.promise(async () => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name }), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const asyncCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(async (id) => { const user = await fetchUser(id); return user.name })))

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk inside a data-last Effect.flatMap in a `.pipe(...)` chain.
// Quick fix: Effect.forEach(xs, (id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" })
export const inPipeFlatMap = Effect.succeed(ids).pipe(Effect.flatMap((xs) => Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(xs.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: reported, but outside the thunk-safe shape, so no quick fix.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: identifier callback (xs.map(fetchUser)); no quick fix.
export const identifierCallback = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST TRIGGER: map callback declares 3 parameters; no quick fix. Effect.forEach passes only
// (item, index), so a callback that declares a third parameter does not type-check after the rewrite.
export const mapWithArrayParam = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id, i, all) => fetchUser(`${i}/${all.length}:${id}`))))

// MUST TRIGGER: `.map` is not Array.prototype.map; no quick fix. The receiver is not iterable,
// so `Effect.forEach(idPage, ...)` would not compile.
export const nonArrayMap = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(idPage.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: argument is an array variable, not xs.map(...); no quick fix.
export const arrayVariable = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: tuple with a rest element (`[...Promise<User>[], Promise<User>]`); no quick fix.
export const restTupleSpread = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([...ids.map(fetchUser), extra]))

// MUST TRIGGER: declared non-empty tuple type (`readonly [Promise<User>, ...Promise<User>[]]`).
export const restTupleDeclared = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(nonEmptyPending))

// MUST TRIGGER: async thunk; no quick fix.
export const asyncThunk = Effect.tryPromise(async () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: block-bodied thunk; the call is not the whole (concise) body, no quick fix.
export const blockBodyThunk = Effect.promise(() => {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the Promise.all result is chained, so the call is not the whole body; no quick fix.
export const chainedResult = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))).then((values) => values.length))

// MUST TRIGGER: { try, catch } object form of Effect.tryPromise; no quick fix.
export const tryPromiseObject = Effect.tryPromise({
  try: () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled with an inline callback still gets no quick fix
// (the success type would change from PromiseSettledResult<A>[]).
export const settledInline = Effect.tryPromise(() => Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id))))

// MUST TRIGGER: global Promise reached through a const alias.
const GlobalPromise = Promise
export const aliasedPromise = Effect.promise(() => GlobalPromise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: other Effect constructor thunks.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.sync thunk.
export const inSync = Effect.sync(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try thunk.
export const inTry = Effect.try(() => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.try { try, catch } object form.
export const inTryObject = Effect.try({
  try: () => Promise.allSettled(pending),
  catch: (cause) => new FetchError({ cause })
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.suspend thunk.
export const inSuspend = Effect.suspend(() => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.callback body.
export const inCallback = Effect.callback<ReadonlyArray<User>>((resume) => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(pending)
  pendingAll.then((values) => resume(Effect.succeed(values)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: thunk nested in a pipeline callback is still a thunk.
export const inForEachCallback = Effect.forEach(
  [ids, mutableIds],
  (group) => Effect.forEach(group, id => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: "unbounded" }),
  { concurrency: 1 }
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.gen and generator Effect.fn bodies.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const inGen = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const promises = ids.map(fetchUser)
  // MUST TRIGGER: bare Promise.all in a gen body (the promises start here, outside the Effect).
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: Promise.allSettled in a gen body.
  const settledAll = Promise.allSettled(promises)
  // MUST TRIGGER: inside an Effect.promise thunk inside the gen body (argument is not xs.map(...), no quick fix).
  const users = yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(promises))
  // MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length tuple in a gen body.
  const pair = Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")])
  return { pendingAll, settledAll, users, pair }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn body.
export const inEffectFn = Effect.fn("inEffectFn")(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fn without a span name.
export const inEffectFnAnonymous = Effect.fn(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled(input.map(fetchUser)))
})

// MUST TRIGGER: generator Effect.fnUntraced body.
export const inEffectFnUntraced = Effect.fnUntraced(function*(input: ReadonlyArray<string>) {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
  return yield* Effect.promise(() => pendingAll)
})

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: fixed-length fan-out (tuple without a rest element).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: two-element literal is a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPair = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: allSettled over a fixed tuple.
export const fixedPairSettled = Effect.promise(() => Promise.allSettled([fetchUser("a"), load()]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `as const` fixed tuple.
export const fixedAsConst = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([fetchUser("a"), fetchUser("b")] as const))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: empty tuple.
export const fixedEmpty = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all([]))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: v1 only reports arrays and rest tuples; a Set is neither.
export const fromSet = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(pendingSet))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: `any` input is neither an array nor a tuple.
export const fromAny = Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(anything))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: outside Effect-run code.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: top-level module code.
export const topLevel = Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: plain async function.
export async function plainAsync() {
  return Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): combinator inside a function nested in the thunk;
// the effect-context analysis resets at every function boundary.
export const nestedInThen = Effect.tryPromise(() => load().then(() => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => fetchUser(id)))))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER (deliberate in v1): function nested in a gen body.
export const nestedInGenCallback = Effect.gen(function*() {
  const run = () => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser))
  return yield* Effect.promise(run)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the thunk returns a function; Promise.all runs in that inner function.
export const thunkReturningFunction = Effect.sync(() => () => Promise.all(pending))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free thunk; only direct thunk arguments are Effect context.
export const pointFreeThunk = pipe(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)), Effect.promise)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: non-generator Effect.fn body is not an Effect context.
export const nonGeneratorEffectFn = Effect.fn("nonGeneratorEffectFn")((input: ReadonlyArray<string>) => {
  const pendingAll = Promise.all(input.map(fetchUser))
  return Effect.promise(() => pendingAll.then((values) => values.length))
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.runPromise wraps an Effect; Promise.all here is plain Promise code.
export const runOutside = () => Promise.all([Effect.runPromise(users), Effect.runPromise(settled)])
export const runOutsideArray = () => Promise.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.runPromise(Effect.succeed(id))))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: not the global Promise.all / Promise.allSettled.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user function named `all`.
const all = <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => Promise.all(values)
export const userAll = Effect.promise(() => all(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a user object with `all` / `allSettled` methods.
const Batch = {
  all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>): Promise<ReadonlyArray<A>> => globalThis.Promise.all(values),
  allSettled: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.allSettled(values)
}
export const batchAll = Effect.promise(() => Batch.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
export const batchAllSettled = Effect.promise(() => Batch.allSettled(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: a local binding named `Promise` shadows the global.
export const shadowedPromise = (() => {
  const Promise = {
    all: <A>(values: ReadonlyArray<globalThis.Promise<A>>) => globalThis.Promise.resolve(values.length)
  }
  return Effect.promise(() => Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser)))
})()

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: other Promise combinators (out of scope; see promiseRaceInEffect).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.race belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
export const race = Effect.promise(() => Promise.race(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.any belongs to promiseRaceInEffect.
export const anyUser = Effect.promise(() => Promise.any(ids.map(fetchUser)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Promise.resolve over an array is not a fan-out.
export const resolved = Effect.promise(() => Promise.resolve(ids.map((id) => id.length)))

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the issue's good examples.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const goodUsers = Effect.forEach(ids, (id) => Effect.tryPromise(() => fetchUser(id)), { concurrency: 8 })

export const goodSettled = Effect.all(ids.map((id) => Effect.promise(() => fetchUser(id))), {
  concurrency: 8,
  mode: "result"
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: one promise per Effect, the shape the quick fix produces.
export const goodUnbounded = Effect.forEach(
  ids,
  (id) => Effect.promise((signal) => fetchUserWithSignal(id, signal)),
  { concurrency: "unbounded" }
)
